subject: Evaluation & MAP: closure conditions, probe test catalog, and signoff path
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Turner <jason.turner@medisure.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation & MAP: closure conditions, probe test catalog, and signoff path

Jason —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As promised, I put together a compact mutual action plan (MAP) draft and a short probe-test catalog to make the evaluation deterministic and easy to operationalize. Attaching the MAP-draft.xlsx and a slim probe-test-cases.md that maps tests to acceptance criteria.

High-level ask: can we align on a small set of exit gates so your team can go from POC -> procurement -> Reserved capacity (if accepted) without surprises? My proposal below is intentionally pragmatic: three gating buckets (Safety & Compliance, Quality & Accuracy, Performance & Stability).

Proposed exit gates (least friction first):
- Safety & Compliance: SOC2 evidence provided OR SOC2 in-progress with expected completion date; PHI redaction probe passes critical cases (see probe-test-cases.md)
- Quality & Accuracy: intent-detection F1 >= 0.88 on our shared validation set; top-1 answer correctness >= 90% on the curated 120-case clinical QA set
- Performance & Stability: 95th percentile latency <= 220ms for 512-token generation on Dedicated profile; sustained throughput >= 6 rps per GPU under guided load (see test harness)

Acceptance tests we suggest running during the 2-week evaluation (dates proposed below):
- Smoke suite (automated): endpoint health, basic prompt/response conformance, byte-level logging verification
- Probe tests (manual + automated): PHI redaction checks, hallucination spot-checks across 20 high-risk prompts, embedding similarity sanity on 500 samples
- Stress run: 30-minute soak at target concurrency to validate autoscaling triggers and KV-cache behavior

Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx (timeline & milestones), probe-test-cases.md (test catalog and pass/fail thresholds).

Proposed timeline:
- 6/12: agree on final MAP and acceptance thresholds
- 6/18: complete smoke & probe tests (first run)
- 6/20: procurement to return SOW or redlines
- 6/25: decision meeting to either sign SOW or identify remaining blockers

If this looks good, I’ll lock the MAP and create a shared folder with the test harness and datasets.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com)

Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), probe-test-cases.md (text)
From: Jason Turner <jason.turner@medisure.io>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@medisure.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP: closure conditions, probe test catalog, and signoff path

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear layout. A few clarifications from our side before we commit to the timeline:

1) Data residency / logs: can the test harness be pointed at our EU VPC instance for the probe tests? We need audit logs to remain in-region.
2) SOC2: we have a copy of your SOC2 in progress notes — can you supply the evidence artifact summary (not the full report) and the targeted completion date?
3) PHI redaction: please add specific probe cases for high-risk entities (MRNs, SSNs disguised in notes). We will run those through our internal DLP too.
4) SLA: 95th p95 latency target is great — can we get a brief note on fallbacks (if Dedicated capacity is short) and whether you can guarantee a 99.9% availability for the evaluation window?

I've attached a short security questionnaire (security-qa.pdf) that procurement asked us to fill before we move to SOW.

If we can get quick answers on the three items above we can commit to the 6/18 probe-run target.

Best,
Jason Turner
Head of Platform & Integrations | MediSure Health
jason.turner@medisure.io

Attachment: security-qa.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Turner <jason.turner@medisure.io>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP: closure conditions, probe test catalog, and signoff path

Jason —

Thanks for the quick review. Short answers and what we’ll do: 

- Data residency/logs: yes — the probe harness can run against your EU VPC. We will stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket in-region; we will not retain copies in our hosted bucket. I will add the exact logging keys and retention policy to the MAP spreadsheet.

- SOC2 evidence: we can provide the summary artifact (scope, test dates, control set, and remediation notes) by EOD 6/12. Full report is under NDA but the summary satisfies your procurement screen.

- PHI redaction probes: attached probe-test-cases.md includes five high-risk scenarios (MRN in text, embedded SSNs, multi-line clinical notes with PHI in headers). For each case we define stimulus, expected redaction behavior, and a fail definition (e.g., any exposed 6+ digit numeric sequence tagged as MRN triggers fail).

Technical acceptance thresholds (concrete):
- Intent detection F1 >= 0.88 (evaluation set: 1,200 labeled utterances)
- Clinical QA top-1 precision >= 90% on curated 120-case set
- Embedding avg cosine > 0.85 on semantic-similarity benchmark (500 pairs)
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms at 512 tokens on Dedicated GPU profile; fallback to Compatible-Quantized variant if Dedicated capacity dips — we will throttle new sessions and return causality headers so you can monitor degrade levels

We will also provide an automated smoke-run harness (bash + pytest) and a reproducible dataset crate (no PHI in the shared crate; sensitive cases will be run behind your VPC).

On availability: for the 2-week evaluation window we can promise 99% uptime for hosted endpoints and a 99.9% target if you take the Dedicated reserved node for that window. Specific SLA text will be included in the SOW.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com)

Jason —

Great — thanks to Karthik for the technical detail. To keep momentum, here is a single-line summary of agreed exit gates and the lightweight acceptance checklist we will use at the end of the run. If anything here looks off, flag inline.

Agreed exit gates (pass = meets threshold OR documented mitigation & timeline):
1) Safety & Compliance — pass if SOC2 summary delivered by 6/12 AND PHI redaction probe passes all 5 high-risk cases when run inside your VPC (pass/fail defined in probe-test-cases.md)
2) Quality & Accuracy — pass if intent F1 >= 0.88 AND clinical QA top-1 >= 90% on the curated sets
3) Performance & Stability — pass if latency p95 <= 220ms on Dedicated profile OR documented fallback plan with measured degraded latency and an agreed mitigant

Acceptance checklist (end-of-eval deliverables):
- Smoke-run report (automated harness output)
- Probe-test results CSV + failing case list (if any)
- Audit log export for test window in your in-region bucket
- SOC2 summary artifact
- Updated MAP-draft.xlsx with final timelines and owners

Next steps & owners: 
- Rachel: finalize MAP and drop final folder (drive link) by EOD 6/12
- Karthik: deliver smoke-run harness + runbook and SOC2 summary by EOD 6/12
- Jason / Procurement: confirm SOW redlines by 6/20 (Procurement contact: procurement@medisure.io)
- Ben: coordinate a technical cutover rehearsal on 6/17 (15–30 min) to validate keys and access

We’ll hold the decision meeting 6/25 at 11:00 PT to review results and next steps; calendar invite to follow once SOW status is known. If everything passes, I’ll include the SOW and DocuSign link in that thread so we can move to signature quickly.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth run.

Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com)
